name: whisper.cpp
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C/C++, our C + C++/libc++ wasi-sdk lane). Core is plain C/C++ with NO codegen/configure: just include/whisper.h + src/whisper.cpp atop the ggml library (ggml.c, ggml-cpu, ggml-alloc, ggml-backend) — "Plain C/C++ implementation without dependencies" for CPU builds. No SDL2/FFmpeg/OpenBLAS needed (those are optional). Build examples/cli (whisper-cli) as the entrypoint reading a model + WAV. Compile with wasi-sdk targeting wasm32-wasi, single-threaded: set GGML_NO_OPENMP / force n_threads=1 and stub/disable pthreads (whisper.cpp has a single-thread fallback). Enable WASM SIMD (-msimd128) — ggml has a WASM_SIMD 128-bit intrinsic path used by the official wasm build. Link libc++ (heavy C++). Models are content-addressed ggml-format bytes (e.g. ggml-tiny.en/base.en) loaded from the sandbox FS via WASI fd; audio fed as 16kHz mono PCM/WAV bytes. Precedent: Agniva (2023) compiled whisper.cpp to WASI single-threaded and successfully transcribed audio on a CPU-only host (wazero), confirming no GPU/network/browser dependency — only model bytes + PCM. Expect slowness (SIMD-only, ~3-5x native) but functionally correct.
smoke: echo "wb run whisper-cli -m /models/ggml-tiny.en.bin -f /audio/jfk.wav -nt -t 1" ; expect stdout transcript line "And so my fellow Americans, ask not what your country can do for you" for the bundled 11s jfk.wav sample shipped in whisper.cpp/samples/.
blocker: Large C++ build atop ggml: requires libc++ lane (have it) and disabling/stubbing pthreads + OpenMP (set n_threads=1, GGML_NO_OPENMP); SIMD path needs -msimd128. Single-threaded + SIMD-only means slow inference (use tiny/base models). Model+audio must be staged into sandbox FS as bytes. No codegen/configure blocker. Not a one-shot compile — non-trivial integration effort, but proven feasible (Agniva ran it standalone single-thread on a non-browser CPU WASI host).

name: ort
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. ort is a thin Rust FFI wrapper over the ONNX Runtime C/C++ library, so its feasibility equals ONNX Runtime's. ORT is a massive CMake C++ codebase (Lane B-disqualifying: codegen/configure, threading, optional GPU EPs). Its ONLY WebAssembly target is the emscripten build (ONNX Runtime Web) which emits .wasm + mandatory JS glue and is browser/Node-oriented — not a plain wasm32-wasi module runnable standalone under wasmtime. ort has no wasm32-wasi feature; on wasm it expects the emscripten ort artifact + JS bindings. Lane A fails (the only prebuilt wasm is emscripten/js-pair, not plain wasm32-wasi). Lane C fails (ort + ORT are enormous, proc-macro/build.rs heavy, link native C++ — mrustc cannot). Lane D N/A. The only in-sandbox ONNX path would be a different crate (tract, pure Rust) or host-brokered wasi-nn — neither is ort.
smoke: N/A — cannot build/run ort as wasm32-wasi. (If a pure-Rust alt were scouted: tract loading a small .onnx and running inference; not applicable to ort.)
blocker: ONNX Runtime's only wasm build is emscripten (ONNX Runtime Web) — .wasm + mandatory JS glue, browser/Node-targeted, NOT plain wasm32-wasi. No standalone wasmtime artifact exists. ort just FFI-wraps that native C++ library; it has no wasm32-wasi target. Native C++ codegen/threading/EPs (Lane B out), too large for mrustc (Lane C out), no prebuilt plain-wasi binary (Lane A out).

name: Burn
recipe: No viable in-sandbox lane. Lane A: no prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm is published — Burn's only wasm artifacts are browser-targeted (MNIST demo, wgpu/WebGPU GPU backend, and the no_std burn-flex/ndarray CPU backend compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown, not WASI). Lane C (mrustc ~1.74): impossible — Burn is a large multi-crate Cargo workspace with derive proc-macros (burn-derive), async/runtime machinery, generics over the Backend trait, and heavy deps (ndarray, bytemuck, derive_more). mrustc cannot build a workspace of this size/complexity or its proc-macros. Lanes B/D N/A (not C/C++, not Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — no artifact to run. (Hypothetically: build burn-flex inference example to wasm32-wasip1 with cargo+rustc, then `wasmtime run model.wasm` predicting an MNIST digit — but this requires full from-source Cargo+rustc compilation of a proc-macro workspace, which the sandbox lanes cannot do.)
blocker: Large proc-macro Rust workspace (burn-derive + async runtime + generic backend trait + ndarray/bytemuck deps) is unbuildable by mrustc ~1.74; no prebuilt standalone wasm32-wasi .wasm exists — Burn's wasm targets are browser-only (wasm32-unknown-unknown CPU/flex + wgpu/WebGPU GPU). No C/C++ or Python/JS lane applies.

name: OpenCV
recipe: No viable lane. (A) No prebuilt PLAIN wasm32-wasi .wasm exists — the only official WASM build is Emscripten (opencv.js / opencv-wasm), which targets the browser JS/glue ABI, not wasi-libc; emscripten-built artifacts will not run standalone under wasmtime+WASI. (B) Self-compile is infeasible: OpenCV is a multi-million-LOC C++ project gated behind a large CMake configure step (feature/codec detection, codegen of config headers), it leans on pthreads (parallel_for), and the documented wasi-sdk attempt (issue #490) failed before even configuring OpenCV — far beyond our C/C++ + libc++ in-sandbox lane (no CMake/configure unless pregenerated). (C) Not Rust. (D) Not pure-Python (heavy C/C++ ext) and not JS-on-QuickJS. wasmvision/wasmcv only proves the negative: it keeps OpenCV NATIVE on the host and exposes WIT bindings to guests — i.e., native exec, which is disallowed.
smoke: If a wasm32-wasi opencv .wasm existed: `wasmtime run opencv.wasm -- <in.jpg> blur <out.jpg>` and diff out.jpg against a known-good Gaussian-blur reference. No such standalone module exists to run.
blocker: Only official WASM build is Emscripten/JS (browser ABI, not WASI-standalone). No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm. Self-compile blocked by giant CMake configure + pthreads; documented wasi-sdk build (issue #490) failed at toolchain stage. wasmvision keeps OpenCV native host-side (disallowed native exec).

name: Skia
recipe: No viable in-sandbox recipe. Official WASM build (CanvasKit) is Emscripten-only and ships as a JS+wasm pair (canvaskit.js loader + canvaskit.wasm), disqualifying Lane A (must be plain wasm32-wasi, not emscripten/js-pair). Lane B from source is infeasible: Skia is a multi-million-LOC C++ tree built with GN/Ninja and a custom emsdk toolchain (//bin/activate-emsdk), pulling ICU, freetype, harfbuzz, libpng/jpeg/webp, expat. Not self-contained C/C++ compilable in our clang+libc++ lane within scope. The only wasm32-wasi reports are hobbyist WASI-SDK experiments running WebGL2 under wasm32-wasip1-threads in a browser (GPU + native-threads + browser context) — not a standalone CPU-raster module under wasmtime. Lanes C/D N/A (C++ project, not Rust crate / pip / JS).
smoke: N/A — no obtainable standalone wasm32-wasi artifact to run. (Intended smoke would have been: wasmtime skia_cpu.wasm rendering a 100x100 RGBA buffer with a filled circle and writing it to a PNG via stdout, asserting non-zero pixel count — but no such plain-wasi module exists.)
blocker: No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists: official CanvasKit is an Emscripten JS+wasm pair, and from-source is a GN/Ninja multi-MLOC C++ tree with ICU/freetype/harfbuzz/image-codec deps and a custom emsdk toolchain — outside the self-contained C/C++ lane. WASI variants found require GPU/WebGL2 + native threads + browser.

name: Cairo
recipe: Lane B in theory: cairo image surface is pure-CPU software rasterization to a memory buffer (no display/GPU/net), so it is sandbox-shaped. But it is NOT self-contained C: the image backend requires a separate pixman library, and any text needs freetype+fontconfig (fontconfig pulls expat + filesystem font discovery). Both cairo and pixman build via meson/autotools with LIVE configure-time feature detection (not pregenerated) — directly excluded by Lane B's no-configure rule. No multi-lib pregenerated wasm32-wasi tree exists.
smoke: If ported: link a test that calls cairo_image_surface_create(CAIRO_FORMAT_ARGB32,64,64); cairo_t*cr=cairo_create(surface); set source rgb, cairo_paint, cairo_rectangle+cairo_fill; then cairo_surface_write_to_png to a WASI fd (or read raw stride via cairo_image_surface_get_data) and assert the painted pixel ARGB bytes. Run under wasmtime, no display.
blocker: No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists — all existing WASM ports (cairo-wasm, roozbehid/cairo, DomAmato) are Emscripten/MSVC, not standalone WASI (Lane A excluded). Lane B blocked because it is a multi-library stack (cairo+pixman, +freetype+fontconfig for text) each built with live meson/autotools configure-time detection — not the no-configure single-lib C drop Lane B requires. Substantial port, not a clean lane fit. The 'wasm-cairo' search hits are the unrelated Starknet Cairo language, not the graphics library.

name: TeX / LaTeX
recipe: No viable lane as a drop-in. Lane A FAILS: every known TeX-to-WASM build (SwiftLaTeX, busytex, texlive.js, TeXlyre/texlyre-busytex, TeXlive.net) is compiled with EMSCRIPTEN and ships a JS-pair (.js + .data glue, web workers) for browser/Node — confirmed no wasm32-wasi/WASI-SDK artifact, no wasmtime support. Not a plain wasm32-wasi .wasm. Lane B FAILS the self-contained bar: TeX engine is web2c-generated (tex.web -> WEB tangle -> C is a CODEGEN step) and the TeX Live tree is autotools ./configure-driven; engine also depends on kpathsea path lib + the texmf data tree (fonts/macros/.fmt formats). That is a multi-hour configure+codegen-coupled build, not a pregenerated self-contained C drop-in. Lanes C (Rust) and D (Python/JS) N/A.
smoke: If a wasm32-wasi pdftex.wasm existed: printf '\\documentclass{article}\\begin{document}hi\\end{document}' > t.tex && wasmtime run --dir=. pdftex.wasm -- -interaction=nonstopmode t.tex (expect t.pdf produced). No such .wasm is available, so this cannot run today.
blocker: All existing TeX WASM builds are emscripten JS-pair (browser/Node), not plain wasm32-wasi runnable under wasmtime. Self-build path is blocked by web2c codegen + autotools ./configure + kpathsea + required texmf data tree — exceeds Lane B's pregenerated/self-contained constraint. Not in the LIVE set.

name: Poetry
recipe: N/A — Poetry is pure-Python and would technically import under the already-live CPython.wasm lane (lane D), but its function is network- and subprocess-bound, not computational.
smoke: poetry --version (works as a no-op); but poetry lock / poetry install / poetry add <pkg> all require reaching PyPI over the network and shelling out to create virtualenvs + invoke PEP 517 build backends — none of which work in-sandbox.
blocker: Network-purpose tool: Poetry's entire reason for existing is resolving and fetching package metadata/wheels from PyPI over the network, creating virtualenvs via subprocess, and invoking PEP 517 build backends (which may compile native deps). No network + no native exec/subprocess in sandbox = the tool cannot perform its function. Per rules, network-purpose -> impossible. Plain Python is already live for actual computation; Poetry adds nothing runnable here.

name: Pipenv
recipe: N/A — Pipenv is pure Python and would nominally ride the existing CPython.wasm Lane D (python already LIVE), but its entire reason to exist is process orchestration: it creates real virtualenvs and shells out to/forks subprocesses. `pipenv shell` spawns a new shell subprocess with the venv activated; `pipenv run` forks a child process; install/lock shell out to pip and virtualenv as child processes. wasm32-wasi under wasmtime has no fork/exec/subprocess and no shell to activate, so the tool's core verbs cannot execute even though the interpreter runs.
smoke: In-sandbox: `python -m pipenv install requests` (or `pipenv run python -c "print(1)"`). Expect failure at the subprocess/virtualenv-creation step (PermissionError / "No such file or directory" on fork/exec, or virtualenv spawn failure) — never a working venv.
blocker: Hard dependency on process model: creating real virtualenvs and spawning subprocesses/shells (fork/exec/subprocess.Popen, `pipenv shell`/`pipenv run`). wasm32-wasi/wasmtime has no fork/exec/subprocess and no shell. The Python interpreter is already LIVE but Pipenv orchestrates child processes around it, which the sandbox forbids.

name: pdm
recipe: Pure-Python; rides existing CPython.wasm lane (python already LIVE). Install pdm + pure-Python deps (resolvelib, unearth, installer, pyproject-hooks, tomlkit, rich, packaging, platformdirs, dep-logic, blinker, httpx, hishel) into the wasm site-packages; msgpack/truststore fall back to pure-Python or are stubbed; no C-ext build needed. python -m pdm as entrypoint.
smoke: In sandbox: python -m pdm --version (and python -c "import pdm; from pdm.models.versions import Version" ) should print version / import cleanly with zero network. Anything beyond import — pdm add/install/lock/sync — hits PyPI over network and spawns subprocess venv/PEP517 builds, which will fail.
blocker: pdm's PURPOSE is network package management: every primary command (add/install/lock/sync/update) fetches from PyPI over the network and spawns subprocesses for virtualenv creation + PEP 517 build isolation (sys.executable -m build). No-network + no native-exec sandbox kills the actual functionality. truststore needs native cert-store bindings (no-op in wasm). Only module import and trivially-offline subcommands (--version, --help, local pyproject/lockfile parse) work — not the tool's value prop.

name: RubyGems (gem)
recipe: No new lane needed — Ruby is ALREADY LIVE. RubyGems ships inside the CRuby interpreter and stdlib; the official ruby.wasm wasm32-wasi build (ruby/ruby.wasm releases, e.g. ruby-3.x-wasm32-unknown-wasi-full.tar.gz) bundles `gem` plus the rubygems stdlib. Since the live `ruby` wasm32-wasi module already includes it, `gem` is reachable today: invoke the existing ruby module with argv `gem`. Pure-Ruby gems install over a VFS-mounted GEM_HOME; only native-extension gems (C build) and network-fetch (`gem install` over RubyGems.org) are out of reach in-sandbox. Local .gem files and pure-Ruby gems work.
smoke: ruby.wasm module, argv=["gem","--version"] -> prints RubyGems version (e.g. 3.5.x); also ruby -e 'require "rubygems"; puts Gem::VERSION' prints same.
blocker: gem install from rubygems.org needs network (not a sandbox purpose); native-extension gems need a C build at install time. Pure-Ruby gems + local .gem install fine offline.

name: Bundler
recipe: Bundler ships inside CRuby/RubyGems; Ruby is already LIVE in-sandbox as ruby.wasm (wasm32-wasi, wasmtime). No separate build needed — Bundler's library is on $LOAD_PATH with stdlib. ruby.wasm explicitly supports RubyGems/Bundler (PR #358). Invoke via `require "bundler/setup"` or `Bundler::CLI.start([...])` from a Ruby entrypoint, mapping the Gemfile dir with --mapdir. Resolver (molinillo) is pure Ruby. Lockfile resolution/generation runs from a local gem source/cache. Network ops (`bundle install` fetching remote gems) are out — no WASI networking.
smoke: printf 'source "https://rubygems.org"\ngem "rake"\n' > Gemfile && wasmtime run --mapdir /work::. --env BUNDLE_GEMFILE=/work/Gemfile --dir . ruby.wasm -- -e 'require "bundler"; puts Bundler::VERSION; d=Bundler::Definition.build("/work/Gemfile",nil,nil); puts d.dependencies.map(&:name).inspect' — expect Bundler version string + ["rake"], proving the pure-Ruby Bundler API loads and parses/resolves a Gemfile offline.
blocker: Network-dependent ops (`bundle install` fetching from rubygems.org, `bundle update`) are impossible in-sandbox — no WASI networking, same as gem. Offline lockfile resolution/parsing against a local gem cache works. Vendored-gem flows need gems pre-mounted via --mapdir.

name: LevelDB
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C++ via our clang/libc++ lane). No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (existing "leveldb wasm" = emscripten/JS+IndexedDB pairs like level-js, NOT standalone wasi — Lane A fails). Build steps: (1) Compile core C++ (db/, table/, util/) with clang++ -target wasm32-wasi. CMake not needed — sources are a flat file list, compile directly. (2) Build WITHOUT compression: leave HAVE_SNAPPY/HAVE_ZSTD undefined (compression is fully optional, port returns false). (3) The blocker is the POSIX Env + port: util/env_posix.cc spawns background compaction via detached std::thread, and port/port_stdcxx.h wraps real std::mutex/std::condition_variable — none of which link/function under single-threaded wasm32-wasi (no wasi-threads/shared-memory in standard wasmtime). Provide a custom single-threaded Env (subclass leveldb::Env): map RandomAccessFile/WritableFile/SequentialFile to WASI open/pread/write/fsync; mmap limiter set to 0; file locks (fcntl) become no-ops (single process). Make Schedule() run the work function INLINE (synchronous compaction) instead of dispatching to a thread, and supply a no-op/std::mutex-free port (Mutex/CondVar as no-ops since single-threaded). This custom-Env path is the documented extension point (Env abstraction), so it's clean work, not a hack — but it IS real porting, not flag-flipping.
smoke: In-sandbox under wasmtime: open a DB at /tmp/testdb (Options.create_if_missing=true), Put("k1","v1") and Put("k2","v2"), Get("k1") returns "v1", iterate forward and confirm sorted order k1<k2, Delete("k1"), Get("k1") returns NotFound. Close, reopen the same path, Get("k2") still returns "v2" (durability across reopen). All without spawning any thread.
blocker: POSIX Env uses detached std::thread for background compaction and port_stdcxx.h uses real std::mutex/std::condition_variable — these do not link/function under single-threaded wasm32-wasi (no wasi-threads in standard wasmtime). Not HAVE_* gated; requires authoring a custom single-threaded Env + thread-free port that runs Schedule() inline. Feasible (Env is the documented seam) but non-trivial porting, not a prebuilt drop-in.

name: ReScript
recipe: No viable in-sandbox lane. ReScript's bsc compiler is OCaml, distributed as native binaries (built via OCaml toolchain + ninja) — no native exec in sandbox (Lane B requires C/C++, not OCaml). The only WASM artifact is the playground bundle produced by js_of_ocaml (JSOO) / experimental wasm_of_ocaml: a BROWSER-hosted target (JS+wasm-gc pair, JS host imports, loads cmij runtime files) — explicitly disqualified as a js-pair/browser build, not plain wasm32-wasi for wasmtime. Lane A fails (no plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists). Lane D (the playground JS bundle on QuickJS) is not a clean fit: it is a multi-MB OCaml-bytecode-to-JS blob built around browser/Node module loading and cmij fetching, not authored for a bare QJS host; would be a heavyweight, fragile integration, not a drop-in.
smoke: N/A — no obtainable wasm32-wasi artifact. (Were a hypothetical bsc.wasm to exist: `wasmtime run bsc.wasm -- -bs-cmi test.res` printing emitted JS for `let x = 1`.)
blocker: Compiler is OCaml; the only WASM build is js_of_ocaml/wasm_of_ocaml — a browser-hosted JS+wasm-gc pair with JS host imports and cmij runtime loading, NOT a standalone wasm32-wasi module runnable under wasmtime. Native binaries need native exec (unavailable). No plain wasm32-wasi artifact exists.

name: Oberon (OBNC)
recipe: OBNC is an Oberon-07 -> C translator implemented in C (mirror: https://github.com/oberonforall/obnc). Build path under our C/C++ lane: (1) the compiler core ships pre-translated C (no Oberon bootstrap binary needed) + a small C runtime + the 7 Oakwood basic-library modules; (2) the HARD dependency is the Boehm-Demers-Weiser GC, which does NOT build cleanly for wasm32-wasi (it relies on threads/sigaltstack/mmap + stack-bottom scanning). To land this in-sandbox you must replace GC with a trivial bump/leak allocator (NEW/NEWARR -> arena malloc, never freed) -- safe because sandbox Oberon programs are short-lived; this is a known small patch (~the GC_malloc shim). (3) OBNC's build uses configure-style host detection -- must be bypassed with a fixed wasi config header (it only probes libc traits, not codegen, so pregeneration is feasible). (4) Generated programs need only standard libc (stdio/stdlib/string) + the GC shim -> our libc/libc++ wasi lane covers it. Two-stage pipeline once built: oberon .Mod -> obnc-compile -> .c -> our existing clang.wasm C lane -> .wasm. So Oberon effectively rides on top of the already-LIVE clang/LLVM lane.
smoke: echo 'MODULE Hello; IMPORT Out; BEGIN Out.String("hello oberon"); Out.Ln END Hello.' > Hello.Mod; obnc Hello (translates to C, compiles via clang.wasm lane, links libc+GC-shim) -> run Hello.wasm under wasmtime -> expect stdout "hello oberon". Validates: Oberon parse -> C emit -> clang wasi compile -> Out.String/Ln stdlib + allocator path.
blocker: Boehm GC dependency does not build for bare wasm32-wasi (threads/sigaltstack/stack-scan); requires swapping in a leak/arena allocator shim. Plus configure-at-build host detection must be replaced with a fixed wasi config header. Both are real (small) porting tasks, not a drop-in. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (only emscripten/JS Oberon emulators, which are browser/JS-pair = out of scope). Until the GC shim + fixed config are proven to build, this is not confirmed live.

name: Io
recipe: Build from IoLanguage/io master (the wasm32-wasi-first branch; native CMake path moved to `native` branch / 2026.04.20-native-final tag). Pure self-contained C via our C/wasi-sdk lane, no configure/codegen needed at build time (IoVMInit.c is pregenerated by io2c and checked in; `make regenerate` is dev-only). Compile sources from libs/basekit/source, libs/garbagecollector/source, libs/iovm/source, deps/parson, deps/libtommath, tools/source with --sysroot=<wasi-sysroot> -msimd128 -O2 -fno-exceptions; link -lwasi-emulated-process-clocks -lwasi-emulated-signal -static to produce build/bin/io_static (WASI CLI). No external libs (libffi/pcre absent; JSON=vendored parson, bignum=vendored libtommath). The setjmp/ucontext coroutine wrinkle is GONE: upstream reimplemented IoCoroutine.c as explicit Io-level frame-chain switching on the single main C stack (header comment: 'no ucontext, fibers, setjmp'), so message/coroutine semantics work without stack-switching or asyncify. Not in the already-live set.
smoke: wasmtime build/bin/io_static -e '"hello" println'  → prints hello. Deeper: wasmtime build/bin/io_static -e 'List clone append(30,10,5,20) sort println' → list(5, 10, 20, 30); and a Coroutine yield/resume one-liner to confirm the frame-chain scheduler.
blocker: None material. Upstream master already targets plain wasm32-wasi with wasi-sdk and runs io_static under wasmtime (our exact host) — confirmed in README Building/Running and Makefile. Only nuance: must build from `master` (not the legacy `native`/CMake branch), and the browser/io_browser.wasm reactor + Io↔JS bridge are browser-only extras we ignore (CLI io_static is the standalone WASI target). DynLib/Eerie addon system is dropped on wasm — irrelevant to a standalone interpreter.

name: Marko
recipe: npm-resolve+bundle @marko/compiler@5.39.63 (pure JS, Babel-based: @babel/core/parser/traverse/generator — no node-gyp/.node/prebuilt binaries) via our esbuild/npm lane into a single JS bundle; load under QuickJS (qjs, already LIVE). Run AOT compile slice only: feed a .marko template string to compiler.compileSync(src, filename, {output:'html'|'dom'}) -> emit plain JS string. Same model as Svelte's compiler. Streaming SSR runtime (@marko/run, server) is OUT — that wants a network-purpose server; only the template->JS compile transform runs in-sandbox.
smoke:
echo a minimal template `
${input.name}
` to a file, then in qjs run the bundled compiler: `compiler.compileSync('
${input.name}
','test.marko',{output:'dom'})` and assert the returned .code is non-empty JS containing the input reference. No filesystem/network needed beyond reading the template string.
blocker: Babel + Marko compiler is a large JS dependency tree; must bundle cleanly (esbuild) and shim any Node builtins (path, fs for source-map/file-frame paths) used by @babel/code-frame and module resolution. QuickJS has no native ESM/Node module system, so resolution must be flattened at bundle time. Risk is bundle size/shim completeness, not feasibility. Compile-only; SSR streaming runtime excluded.

name: Stencil
recipe: No viable lane. Stencil (@stencil/core) is a large Node application, not a single-shot compiler. Its build pipeline bundles native-binary Rollup 4.x (@rollup/rollup-*-{gnu,musl,msvc} .node addons), esbuild, terser, a ws-based dev server, Puppeteer, and file-watching, with engines.node >=16. The transform leans on Node's process/fs/net runtime, a baked-in HTTP/WebSocket dev server and live-reload watcher — none of which exist under plain wasm32-wasi on wasmtime. Lane A: no prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi exists. Lane B/C: N/A (JS/TS project). Lane D (JS on QuickJS/esbuild): the inner TS->WC transform is JS, but @stencil/core as shipped is a multi-MB Node app with native deps and a network dev server; isolating a pure in-memory AOT transform would be a full from-scratch port, not packaging. Out of scope for the no-full-compile bar.
smoke: N/A — cannot produce a standalone wasm32-wasi artifact to smoke-test. (Aspirational only: feed a .tsx component to an isolated transpile under qjs and assert it emits a customElements.define bundle — not achievable without porting Stencil's compiler off Node.)
blocker: Node-oriented build app: native-binary Rollup, esbuild, terser, ws dev server + live-reload file watcher, Puppeteer; engines.node>=16. Relies on process/fs/net + a network dev-server purpose. No single-shot in-memory compiler; no plain wasm32-wasi artifact. Network/dev-server purpose + native deps make it impossible without a full from-scratch port.

name: Enhance (@enhance/ssr render core)
recipe: Lane D (JS-on-qjs via the runtime's npm/esbuild bundle lane). Scope: the @enhance/ssr render core ONLY (pure custom-element -> HTML-string expansion), NOT the Arc/Begin Lambda server, router, or file-watching. Steps: (1) npm install @enhance/ssr@4.0.3 — pure-JS tree only: @begin/parse5 -> parse5@7 -> entities (HTML parser, pure JS) + nanoid@4. No *.node / binding.gyp / native addons. (2) Bundle with esbuild: `esbuild app.mjs --bundle --format=iife --platform=browser --conditions=browser`. The `browser` condition resolves nanoid to index.browser.js, which uses WebCrypto `crypto.getRandomValues` instead of Node's `crypto.randomFillSync`. Result: ~343KB pure-ES bundle with ZERO residual Node builtins (verified: no require("fs|http|net|crypto|path|os"), no node: specifiers). (3) Run on qjs lane with two shims only: `print` and `crypto.getRandomValues` (the qjs npm lane already provides such WebCrypto shims). nanoid is additionally injectable via enhance's `uuidFunction` option, so a getRandomValues shim isn't even strictly required.
